description: Standard proof artifact expectations by sprint type. Defines what must be in a proof bundle for each category of sprint work.

sprint_types.description: Documentation-only sprints — governance, architecture docs, contracts, READMEs

required_proof.description: TypeScript compilation still passes (no doc changes broke imports)

optional_proof.description: Lint check for any code formatting in docs

sprint_types.ratification_threshold: All required artifacts present. Typecheck passes. Diff shows only doc file changes.
sprint_types.notes: Docs sprints have the lowest proof burden. The main risk is inadvertent code changes — diff review confirms scope.

sprint_types.description: Sprints that change runtime behavior — agents, data pipelines, API logic, settlement

required_proof.description: Single-writer gate passes (if unified_picks in scope)
Database state, API response, or log output showing correct runtime behavior
Sprint summary with runtime evidence summary

sprint_types.ratification_threshold: All required artifacts present. Typecheck and tests pass. Build succeeds. Runtime evidence demonstrates correct behavior. Lifecycle gate passes if applicable.
sprint_types.notes: Runtime sprints have the highest proof burden. Build-time evidence alone is insufficient — runtime proof is mandatory.

sprint_types.description: Sprints that fix build errors, type errors, lint issues, or dependency problems

required_proof.description: TypeScript compilation passes (this IS the fix evidence)
Tests still pass after build fix
Sprint summary showing before/after build state

optional_proof.description: Lint output if lint was part of the fix

sprint_types.ratification_threshold: All required artifacts present. Typecheck and build pass. Tests pass. Diff confirms changes are limited to build-fix scope.
sprint_types.notes: Build-fix sprints demonstrate the fix via the build/typecheck passing. Before-state should be documented in closeout report.

sprint_types.description: End-to-end lifecycle sprints — spanning ingestion through settlement

required_proof.description: Full test suite results including lifecycle tests
Database state showing full lifecycle flow (submit -> grade -> promote -> post -> settle)
Sprint summary with e2e flow verification

sprint_types.ratification_threshold: All required artifacts present. Full test suite passes. Lifecycle gate passes. Runtime evidence shows complete e2e flow. Discord delivery verified. No deprecated path usage.
sprint_types.notes: E2E lifecycle sprints have maximum proof requirements. Every stage of the lifecycle must be evidenced.

sprint_types.description: UI sprints — command-center, dashboard, or smart-form changes

required_proof.description: Sprint summary with UI change description

sprint_types.ratification_threshold: All required artifacts present. Typecheck and build pass. UI changes are visually verified (screenshots recommended). Diff confirms scope.
sprint_types.notes: UI sprints that also modify data submission (smart-form -> bridge_outbox) upgrade to T3 and require runtime evidence.

sprint_types.description: Database schema migrations — new tables, columns, constraints, triggers

required_proof.description: TypeScript compilation passes with new types
Migration SQL captured in diff with rollback documented
Sprint summary with migration description and rollback documentation

optional_proof.description: Database query showing schema change applied correctly
Lifecycle gate if schema change affects unified_picks

sprint_types.ratification_threshold: All required artifacts present. Typecheck and build pass. Schema matches types. Migration has documented rollback. Tests pass.
sprint_types.notes: Schema sprints are high-risk because migrations are effectively irreversible in production. Rollback documentation is mandatory.
